contrast: v475: in possessive_number the model RESISTED a number attractor on 32/32 rows. Two families, opposite results -- recency governs PP selection from a noun cue, but not number agreement.
instrument: CPU capability screen (g.prepare valid_only=True); no GPU battery -- the screen alone adjudicates
registered_reading: A recency reader and a governance reader predict OPPOSITE tokens on every row of the distractor cell, so a full drop IS the recency finding. The neutral-distractor cell holds the frame, length, cue pair, suffix and readout pair fixed and changes one word, so it separates 'follows the nearest noun' from 'this frame is too heavy'.
result: competing cue noun: 32/32 rows dropped on BOTH A1 and A2. neutral distractor, same frame: 0/32 dropped, margins +/-0.8. One word differs between the two cells, so the collapse is attributable to the competing cue noun and not to the frame: THE MODEL FOLLOWS THE NEAREST NOUN.
scope: Behavioural, not causal. It says the model is a recency reader for this behaviour, and therefore that in this family 'the cue' and 'the nearest noun' cannot be separated behaviourally at all -- which bounds what any circuit here can be claimed to be. It does not say what a fitted direction encodes.
